newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper to thrust higher, but market wary.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper to thrust higher, but market wary.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper may extend Thursday's spike higher, but players are nervous of a reversal around $2,300 a tonne or at next resistance around $2,340/50.
Aluminium is also back at the top end of its recent range but analysts and traders are not sure it has the momentum to break through ceilings at $1,585 and $1,606.
COPPER -
The market might have more scope on the upside, but the threat of further weighty stocks rises could cause players to turn tail.
Stocks increased by 13,025 tonnes on Thursday after 17,025 tonnes the previous day.
Resistance on any jump higher would be seen at $2,300 and then around the Tuesday peak of $2,337.
Analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said the market would initially see signs of strength, but the upside was limited.

"As stocks continue to find their way into LME warehouses...even with copper's critical commercial stock situation, the upside potential becomes increasingly limited," he said, adding that spikes would provide good selling opportunities.

On the downside, $2,280 was the initial support area, chartist Harry Creates of broker AMT said. "If $2,280 breaks, falls to $2,240 could be seen," he said. Next support was pegged at Thursday's low of $2,226.
At 0750 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,286/90, down about $6 from Thursday's late close.
ALUMINIUM -
The market was stronger after closing near its highs on Thursday.
But it would come up against sticky layers of resistance and might not have enough power to break through, analysts said.
Prices closed just above the 10-day moving average at $1,577 but the 30-day moving average at $1,588, the 40-day average at $1,595 and the psychological $1,600 region would provide upside obstacles.
"The course of action for the time being would be to sell any moves into this shark-infested area," said broker Gerald in a commentary.
Broker Brandeis said, "Resistance immediately overhead is evident and could prove difficult to surmount."
Above $1,600, resistance was pegged at $1,606, then at the July 3 peak of $1,620.
Support was seen at $1,560, then at the recent lows around $1,545.
At 0805 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,580/83, unchanged from Thursday's late close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
